## What I did

Installed syri and minimap2 on to the mutationSynteny conda environment. 

![Screenshot 2026-07-06 at 12.05.02 PM.png](data:image/png;base64,)![Screenshot 2026-07-06 at 12.05.21 PM.png](data:image/png;base64,)

**[conda program name] -h** will give a list of all of the necessary commands that the program has so that you can use them and understand what does what. 

**Commands of importance:** 
The goal is to analyze the mutant line (VA2) vs the control line (VA1) and look at they synteny between the two.

 **-r REF** refers to the Genome A, or the reference genome. This would be VA1 in this case. 
**-q QRY** refers to the Genome B, or the query genome which is comparing against the reference. This would be VA2. 
**-F {B}** refers to the input file type. The default of this is {T} but because we have BAM files we are working with this needs to be switched to B. T=Table, S=SAM, B=BAM, P=PAF (Pairwise mApping File.)

Syri by default filters out low quality and small alignments. Using -f removes this default. May be something to consider because the low quality reads may be SVs from somatic mutations. 

**--nc NCORES** sets the number of cores used in parallel and can be no more than the number of chromosomes (max 5 for Arabidopsis.) 
**--samplename** names the sample name to be in the output VCF files. 

Data wrangling/adjusting commands:
**--invgaplen INVGL** sets the maximum allowed gap length between two alignments of a multialignment inversions. Affects the selection of which inversions can have different lengths between reference and query. Establishes when to consider and inversion two seperate inversions. A higher value can catch real inversion with an unaligned gap, but this also risks merging two independent events. A smaller value avoids false positives, but risks missing if the true gap is larger, and splitting one event into two events.
**--tdgaplen TDGL** similar concept as invgaplen, but works with translocations and duplications. 
**--tdmaxolp TDOLP** Maximum overlap allowed between two translocation/duplication events with a value range between (0,1]. 
**--unic TRANSUNICOUNT** number of unique base pairs for selecting for translocations. Setting for smaller values would find smaller translocations better, but takes more time to compute for and also can decrease accuracy. 
**--unip TRANSUNIPERCENT** percent of unique regions required to select for translocation. Smaller values select for TDs with higher overlap with other regions. 
**--no-chrmatch** Does not allow for syri to automatically match two chromosomes if their genomes are not equal. By default this is off, and should probably stay off. 

**--nosv** skips structural variation identification
**--nosnp** skips all snp/indel indetification
**--all** uses duplications for variant identification as well
**--allow-offset** Base pairs are allowed to overlap
**--hdrseq** Outputs highly divided regions sequence, or the sequences of the rearranged unsyntenic blocks.
